title: Realization of a flat semisimplicial derived system
statement: Use the semisimplicial ringed total category $\mathscr M$, component sites $(\mathcal C_n,\mathcal O_n)$ and module pullbacks of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]. Assume $f_\alpha^*$ is exact for every injection $\alpha:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$ (flatness of the ringed transition). Suppose given $B_n\in D(\mathcal O_n)$ and isomorphisms $\theta_\alpha:Lf_\alpha^*B_m\xrightarrow{\sim}B_n$, compatible with identities and composition through the canonical derived pullback comparisons. If $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_n)}(B_n,B_n[t])=0$ for every $n\ge0$ and every integer $t<0$, there is a cartesian $B\in D(\mathscr M)$ and isomorphisms $e_nB\simeq B_n$ intertwining every $\theta_\alpha$. There is no bound on the cohomological amplitude of the $B_n$ and no quasi-coherence assumption.

proof.text: Use the exact adjoints $j_{r!}\dashv e_r$ of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-evaluation-free-adjoint] and put $X_r=j_{r!}B_r$. For each face $\delta_i:[r-1]\hookrightarrow[r]$, define $d_{r,i}:X_r\to X_{r-1}$ to be adjoint to $B_r\xrightarrow{\theta_{\delta_i}^{-1}}f_{\delta_i}^*B_{r-1}\hookrightarrow e_rX_{r-1}$. Here exactness identifies $Lf_\alpha^*$ with termwise $f_\alpha^*$. Put $d_r=\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^id_{r,i}$. The adjunction formula says that in component $m$ the $\alpha:[r]\hookrightarrow[m]$ summand is carried to the $\alpha\delta_i$ summand by $f_\alpha^*\theta_{\delta_i}^{-1}$. In all formulas use the canonical pullback composition comparisons.

source.place: Tag 0D9T, first proof bullet; Tag 0D9L, first paragraph, replacing all simplex maps by injections

proof.text: We verify $d_{r-1}d_r=0$. For $a<b$, omitting vertices $a,b$ has the two factorizations $\delta_b\delta_a=\delta_a\delta_{b-1}$. Their coefficient maps agree because $\theta_{\alpha\beta}=\theta_\alpha f_\alpha^*\theta_\beta$. Their signs in the double boundary are $(-1)^{a+b}$ and $(-1)^{a+b-1}$, so they cancel. This checks the identity on every summand of every $e_mX_r$; the derived adjunction of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-evaluation-free-adjoint] checks the same equality directly in $D(\mathscr M)$ by evaluating on the identity summand in degree $r$. Thus $(X_r,d_r)$ is a complex in $D(\mathscr M)$.

proof.text:
For $i>j+2$ set $a=i-j-2>0$. By derived adjunction and the finite-sum formula,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(X_i[a],X_j)=\operatorname{Hom}(B_i[a],e_i j_{j!}B_j)\simeq\bigoplus_{\alpha:[j]\hookrightarrow[i]}\operatorname{Hom}(B_i[a],f_\alpha^*B_j).$$
Each $\theta_\alpha$ identifies its target with $B_i$, so every summand is $\operatorname{Hom}(B_i,B_i[-a])=0$. Apply [lem-sfb-countable-postnikov-extension-comparison] successively, starting with $Y_0=X_0$, to obtain a single compatible countable Postnikov system with triangles $Y_r\to X_r\to Y_{r-1}\to Y_r[1]$. Put $E_r=Y_r[r]$ and use its connecting arrows $E_{r-1}\to E_r$.

proof.text: The abelian sheaves on the total site and on every component have exact filtered colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact]. The faithful exact forgetful functors of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] preserve these colimits, hence the module categories have exact filtered colimits too. A countable sum is a filtered colimit of its finite partial sums, so countable sums are exact. Therefore [lem-kun-derived-countable-sums-exact] supplies countable coproducts in the unbounded derived categories, computed on complexes. Choose a telescope $B=\operatorname{hocolim}_r E_r$, namely a cone of $1-\mathrm{successor}$ on $\bigoplus_r E_r$. It exists by the cone axiom in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $b:X_0=E_0\to B$ be its zeroth leg. Evaluation $e_m$ preserves module sums: form their component sums and induced transitions, using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] for $f_\alpha^*\dashv f_{\alpha,*}$ and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] for its preservation of sums; a compatible family of maps from the summands is uniquely a map of systems by [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]. The derived coproduct theorem just cited therefore gives preservation of countable derived sums. Termwise evaluation commutes with shifts and cones, hence is exact by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; [lem-kun-functor-preserves-hocolim] therefore identifies $e_mB$ with a telescope of $e_mE_r$, compatibly with the actual legs and hence with $e_mb$.

proof.text:
Fix $m$. Put $A_{m,r}=\bigoplus_{\alpha:[r]\hookrightarrow[m]}B_m$, zero for $r>m$, with alternating boundary given by precomposition with faces. The maps $v_{m,r}:e_mX_r\simeq A_{m,r}$ are the sums of $\theta_\alpha$. They commute with the boundaries: on the $\alpha$ summand the two maps to the $\alpha\delta_i$ summand are equal by
$$\theta_{\alpha\delta_i}\, f_\alpha^*(\theta_{\delta_i}^{-1})=\theta_\alpha.$$
There is an explicit comparison Postnikov system for this finite complex. Represent $B_m$ by a cochain complex $K_m$. For $r\ge0$ let $T_{m,r}^q=\bigoplus_{0\le n\le\min(r,m)}\bigoplus_{\alpha:[n]\hookrightarrow[m]}K_m^{q+n}$, with differential the face boundary plus $(-1)^n d_{K_m}$ on the $n$th summand. Then $T_{m,r-1}\to T_{m,r}$ is the inclusion of a subcomplex, and its quotient is $A_{m,r}[r]$ represented with the usual shifted differential. The degreewise split short exact sequence and [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] give triangles $T_{m,r-1}\to T_{m,r}\to A_{m,r}[r]\to T_{m,r-1}[1]$; rotation and shifting exhibit $Z_{m,r}=T_{m,r}[-r]$ as a Postnikov system. Explicitly, take $a_r:Z_{m,r}\to A_{m,r}$ to be $(-1)^{r(r-1)/2}$ times top projection and $b_r:A_{m,r}\to Z_{m,r-1}$ to be $(-1)^{r(r+1)/2+1}$ times the face boundary into its top summand. Since $r(r-1)+2$ is even, $a_{r-1}b_r$ is the prescribed boundary. The connecting maps $Z_{m,r-1}\to Z_{m,r}[1]$ are the inclusions of the finite total complexes. These triangles follow by identifying $Z_{m,r}$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(b_r)[-1]$: reorder the two finite blocks and multiply the top block by the displayed sign. This also fixes the maps from $T_{m,0}$ to $T_{m,r}$ as the literal inclusions.

proof.text:
For the two systems $e_mY_r$ and $Z_{m,r}$, the comparison obstruction groups for $i>j+1$ are
$$\operatorname{Hom}(e_mX_i[i-j-1],A_{m,j}).$$
Both arguments are finite sums of $B_m$ up to the indicated shift, so these groups vanish by the negative self-Ext hypothesis (and are zero if $i>m$). The comparison clause of [lem-sfb-countable-postnikov-extension-comparison] extends $v_{m,r}$ to isomorphisms of the systems, in particular $c_m:e_mE_m\simeq T_{m,m}$ compatible with the maps out of $e_mX_0$. Since $e_mX_r=0$ for $r>m$, the Postnikov triangles show $e_mE_{r-1}\to e_mE_r$ is an isomorphism for every $r>m$: the cone is $e_mX_r[r]=0$. By [lem-sfb-sequential-telescope-calculus] the actual leg $\lambda_m:e_mE_m\to e_mB$ is an isomorphism. Thus define $\gamma_m:e_mB\to B_m$ to be $\lambda_m^{-1}$, then $c_m$, then the fold augmentation $\epsilon_m:T_{m,m}\to K_m$ in the derived category. It remains to check that this augmentation is an isomorphism and the $\gamma_m$ intertwine transitions.

source.place: Tag 0D9L, comparison obstruction groups and gamma_m; injective indexing makes the evaluated tower stationary after m

proof.text: The augmentation $\epsilon_m$ is a homotopy equivalence, for any (possibly unbounded) representative $K_m$. Indeed write an increasing simplex as $[v_0,\ldots,v_n]$. On the augmented simplex chain complex set $h[v_0,\ldots,v_n]=[0,v_0,\ldots,v_n]$ if $v_0>0$ and $h=0$ if $v_0=0$, and send the augmented degree $-1$ to vertex $[0]$. Expanding the alternating boundary gives $\partial h+h\partial=1$ in the augmented complex: when $v_0>0$, the first face of $[0,v_0,\ldots,v_n]$ is the original simplex and every other face cancels its term in $h\partial$; when $v_0=0$, only the first face contributes, returning the original simplex. On the nonaugmented total complex this is the identity minus the vertex-zero inclusion followed by the fold. Apply this $h$ to the simplex index and the identity to $K_m$; the vertical terms cancel since $(-1)^{n+1}+(-1)^n=0$. This is a cochain homotopy between $1$ and the vertex-zero inclusion composed with $\epsilon_m$. The opposite composite is $1$ on $K_m$. Therefore $\epsilon_m$ and hence $\gamma_m$ are isomorphisms, with no amplitude bound.
